To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) a commitment statute summary did not improve predictions of dangerousness, and (b) psychiatrists who were given the statute summary and who predicted dangerousness to others based on the case histories were less consistent in these predictions when the patient had an extensive history of violence

the Arizona dangerousness statute, as a legal standard for dangerousness, is not useful for predicting dangerousness to self and others and that it may have an adverse effect on the consistency of dangerousness prediction.

1) the use of the statute definition of dangerousness resulted in less accurate predictions than did the absence of such a definition; and 2) the use of a definition of dangerousness by psychiatrists who were not trained in its use resulted in less accurate judgments than did the use of the same definition by psychiatrists who received special training in its use.
